- owner: AI Governance
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory activity policy
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Scope and approval boundary

This policy covers employees, contractors and teams using AI for Northstar work. Permission is the intersection of activity, exact tool/model/deployment combination, purpose, data class, user population and approval conditions. Approval of an underlying model never authorizes an unlisted endpoint or a new customer-facing deployment. Use REG-002 for asset permissions and AUTH-009 for review authority.

## S02. Permitted everyday assistance

Within an existing approved combination, employees may draft, summarize, brainstorm, analyze permitted aggregate information and obtain code assistance. Routine use within recorded purpose and data limits needs tool access but no new use-case review. Review generated output before using it in a business process or communicating externally.

## S03. Absolute prohibitions

Do not use AI to make autonomous hiring, termination, credit or disciplinary decisions. Do not upload credentials, payment card details, production secrets, individual health records or individual HR performance records to any deployment in this corpus. No exception under PROC-004 may override these prohibitions.

## S04. Customer-facing and custom applications

New customer-facing generation, custom RAG applications, new system integrations and automated consequential advice require documented use-case review. A tool subscription, a pilot designation and sponsor endorsement do not grant production authorization. Release requires an applicable decision plus verified pre-release conditions.

## S05. Account and deployment requirements

Use company-managed identities, approved endpoints and required logging/retention settings. Personal consumer accounts are not permitted for company work. Do not copy an approved model name into an unapproved service and assume permission carries over. Unlisted tools have no documented approval.

## S06. Human accountability

The named employee remains responsible for accuracy, fairness and suitability. Customer communications require a competent reviewer. Generated code follows code review, testing and security checks. Legal interpretations require Legal review. The assistant provides guidance, not a formal approval or legal opinion.

## S07. Data handling

STD-003 determines classification and redaction. Raw personal data is excluded from every currently approved deployment in REG-002. Removing names alone does not establish anonymity. An approved Confidential nonpersonal use does not permit Confidential personal data.

## S08. Material change and renewal

A model-version change, new data class, region, provider, purpose, integration or audience requires change assessment under RSK-006. An earlier decision is scoped to its exact request version; a superseding version must not silently inherit affected reviews or release clearance. Expired, revoked and rejected decisions do not authorize continuing use.

## S09. Conflicts and missing evidence

Apply every relevant restriction. FAQ-005 is illustrative and cannot override authoritative rules. When authoritative sources conflict on the same requirement, identify the conflict, withhold definitive permission and contact the owners. Missing evidence, unknown regional approval and a low similarity score never imply permission.

## S10. Reporting and recordkeeping

Report suspected sensitive-data exposure immediately through Security Incident intake. Do not paste the exposed data into AI Compass. Record approval rationale, source versions and evidence references; log formal actions under AUD-012. Retain records under ENG-007 and PROC-004.

# Data Classification & AI Handling Standard

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 3
- source_id: STD-003
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: Information Security & Privacy
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory data standard
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Classification approach

The data owner assigns the highest applicable class. Evaluate content, context and linkability rather than file extension or size. A summary, embedding or pilot copy does not automatically lower classification. When classification is uncertain, ask the data owner or Security before upload.

## S02. Public

Information formally approved for public release, such as published product guides and public blog posts. It may be processed only in an approved combination for its permitted purpose. Public status does not remove intellectual-property or accuracy-review responsibilities.

## S03. Internal

Routine nonpublic agendas, nonsensitive operating instructions and truly aggregate sales figures without customer-level records. Use company identities and deployments explicitly permitting Internal data. The source owner must confirm that aggregation removes identifiers and small-group reidentification risks.

## S04. Confidential nonpersonal

Nonpublic commercial plans, contracts without personal information, and source code without credentials, secrets or personal information. Only DEP-002 and DEP-003 permit specified Confidential nonpersonal uses; the approved purpose still applies. InsightDesk and Northstar Assist do not permit Confidential data.

## S05. Confidential personal

Customer names, email addresses, identifiable support transcripts and supplier contact details are Confidential personal data unless a higher class applies. All currently approved deployments exclude raw personal data. Privacy review alone does not grant permission where the catalog or policy still prohibits processing.

## S06. Restricted

Credentials, payment card details, production secrets, individual health records and individual HR performance records are Restricted. No registered deployment may process them. The exception route cannot override this rule. Stop upload and involve the data owner or Security.

## S07. Redaction and reassessment

Remove direct identifiers and indirect identifiers, unique account/order references, sensitive free text and details enabling reidentification. Reassess the remaining content with the owner. Routine meeting notes may become Internal only if no Confidential or Restricted information remains. Use synthetic examples when sanitization cannot be established.

## S08. RAG and derived artifacts

Source ACLs and classification apply to extracted text, chunks, embeddings, indexes, reranker inputs, retrieved context, evaluation datasets, traces and exports. Enforce authorization before retrieval and on parent expansion, evidence display and download. Do not expose excluded text to an external judge or reranker.

## S09. Regional scope

Catalog endpoints in this corpus are approved only for their recorded fictional region and environment. No blanket EU, Austria, APAC or cross-border permission is documented. Route regional questions to Privacy, Legal and Architecture; do not infer a legal conclusion.

## S10. Exposure response

If prohibited data was entered into a tool, stop further use, notify Security Incident intake, preserve relevant record identifiers and follow the incident owner instructions. Do not ask an assistant to repeat, recover or redistribute the exposed material.

# AI Access & Exception Procedure

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 4
- source_id: PROC-004
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: AI Governance Operations
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory operating procedure
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Approved-tool access

Submit tool/deployment ID, purpose, manager and intended data categories to IT Service Desk. Check the exact permitted combination first. Access target is two business days after a complete request; service targets are not guarantees or automatic approvals.

## S02. Use-case intake

Provide purpose, requester, sponsor, users, tools, all generation/embedding/reranking model versions, endpoints, hosting region, data classes/flows, oversight, impact and evaluation plan. Submit categories, not raw sensitive examples. Submission freezes a numbered snapshot.

## S03. Triage and information requests

Governance checks completeness, confirms the risk screening and applies AUTH-009. Triage target is three business days after complete intake. Missing information pauses triage or review; the coordinator records the requested fields and accountable owner. Do not treat an overdue target as approval.

## S04. Domain review and blockers

Assigned specialists record satisfactory, changes-requested or blocking findings for a specific request version. They cite requirements and evidence. A domain finding is not final disposition. Required unsatisfactory findings prevent approval; the decision owner cannot silently override them.

## S05. Formal decisions

Only the assigned authorized decision owner records Approved, Approved with conditions, Rejected or Return for revision. Record rationale, exact scope, applicable policy/routing versions, validity and conditions. Requesters may not decide their own cases. A sponsor or administrator has no implied decision authority.

## S06. Exceptions

Name the requirement, business need, compensating control, risk owner, duration and policy owner. Permitted exceptions last at most 90 days and need the decision owner plus affected policy-owner approval. Exceptions cannot permit Restricted data, personal accounts, autonomous prohibited decisions or raw personal data in a deployment that excludes it.

## S07. Evidence and release

Separate pre-release conditions from ongoing obligations. Evidence owners submit versioned artifacts; a distinct assigned verifier inspects them against the exact configuration. Only the release authority clears the case after all pre-release conditions pass. Ongoing monitoring remains required after release.

## S08. Change, renewal, expiry and revocation

Open a new request version for material scope changes. Reopen affected reviews. Renew before the valid-until timestamp; after expiry stop the scoped activity until reauthorization. Security or Governance may revoke an approval through a recorded decision; preserve original history.

## S09. Escalation and incidents

Policy ambiguity: AI Governance Operations. Data classification: data owner or Security. Proposed personal data: Privacy plus catalog-owner assessment. Suspected exposure: Security Incident intake immediately. All named teams and internal routes are fictional service records in this corpus.

## S10. Records, corrections and retention

Keep immutable submitted snapshots and append superseding decisions with reasons. Retain records for 24 months after closure in this fictional schedule, extended by legal hold. Restrict cases and exports by assignment. Record timestamps in UTC. History integrity requires server controls; synthetic hashes are demonstrations only.

## S09. How do I get access to Northstar Assist?

Confirm DEP-001 scope, then send purpose, manager and data categories to IT Service Desk. Target is two business days after complete intake, not a guarantee.

Do not infer approval. Prepare a new-tool/use-case intake and wait for the relevant assessment.

## S11. Can AI make a hiring shortlist from individual performance reviews?

Autonomous hiring decisions are prohibited and individual performance records are Restricted. A case exception cannot authorize the proposal.

## S12. Can we change Vector Pine 1.0 to 1.1 without reapproval?

Governing citations: REG-002@3.0:MOD-008@1.1, REG-002@3.0:DEP-011, ENG-007@3.0:S06.

## S13. Who can give final approval?

The assigned authorized decision owner, after mandatory reviews. Sponsor, coordinator and administrator status alone are insufficient.

Governing citations: PROC-004@3.0:S05, AUTH-009@3.0:S08.

## S14. Can the person uploading evidence verify it too?

No. A distinct assigned independent verifier must inspect the exact artifact/configuration.

Governing citations: PROC-004@3.0:S07, AUTH-009@3.0:S08.

## S15. Does conditional approval mean ready for production?

No. All pre-release conditions must pass and release authority must record clearance. Ongoing obligations continue after release.

Governing citations: AUTH-009@3.0:S09, PROC-004@3.0:S07.

## S16. Can an approved model be used in a new overseas region?

No regional permission can be established from this corpus beyond US-SYN-1. Ask Privacy, Legal and Architecture; do not assume authorization.

Governing citations: STD-003@3.0:S09, REG-002@3.0:S01.

## S17. What if two policies conflict?

Identify the conflicting requirements, abstain from definitive permission and contact the source owners. FAQ examples cannot override authoritative rules.

Governing citations: POL-001@3.0:S09.

## S18. Can I keep using an application after approval expires?

No. Renew before expiration; stop scoped use after expiry until reauthorization.

Governing citations: PROC-004@3.0:S08, AUTH-009@3.0:S09.

## S19. Will a read-only source ACL still apply to embeddings?

Yes. Classification and source permissions apply to chunks, embeddings, retrieval context, reranker inputs and exports.

Governing citations: STD-003@3.0:S08, ENG-007@3.0:S01.

It can assist evaluation, but it cannot act as the authorized human verifier or decision owner. Synthetic fixtures are not proof of actual test execution.

## S01. Screening outcomes

Low: assistance wholly inside an existing approved combination and purpose. Moderate: new internal custom applications or integrations without prohibited data. High: customer-facing generation or material consequential advice requiring accountable human oversight. Prohibited: any activity expressly barred by POL-001. These are fictional enterprise categories, not regulatory classifications.

## S02. Context and accountability

Record affected users, output use, business impact, data lineage, intended oversight and fallback. The assistant may suggest a tier, but Governance confirms screening. Consider the application behavior, not merely the model size or vendor reputation.

## S03. Customer-facing builds

Require sponsor endorsement and Technology, Security, Legal and Compliance/Risk reviews. Add Privacy when personal data is proposed. A missing Privacy assessment blocks a personal-data proposal, and a Privacy finding cannot override a catalog data restriction. Use AUTH-009 rules R02 and R04.

## S04. Internal custom builds

Require sponsor endorsement and Technology and Security reviews. Add Legal for contractual/IP interpretation and Privacy for proposed personal data. Routine existing tool use within scope is not a custom build. Use AUTH-009 rules R01 and R03.

## S05. Model and deployment changes

Evaluate generation, embedding and reranking versions separately. Changing the embedding model requires a separate consistent index and retrieval reevaluation; do not mix vector spaces. Model/provider/endpoint/region changes require a recorded assessment. See ENG-007 S06.

## S06. Conditions and residual risk

Describe compensating controls, owner, evidence, phase, due date and monitoring. A pre-release condition is not satisfied by promising to fix it later. Ongoing obligations remain tracked after clearance. A prohibited activity cannot be downgraded to Low through a pilot or exception.

## S07. Reassessment triggers

New users, data categories, system integration, autonomous behavior, material retrieval/prompt changes, security incidents and expiring authority trigger reassessment. The new snapshot must reference previous versions and identify which reviews remain applicable; affected reviews must be redone.

## S08. Worked screening examples

Public blog drafting in DEP-001: Low. New internal RAG application in proposed DEP-009: Moderate. Existing contract summary in DEP-003 within purpose: Low. Customer support RAG application: High. Confidential nonpersonal code in DEP-002 within purpose: Low. Autonomous hiring selection: Prohibited.

# AI Development, Evaluation & Monitoring Standard

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 7

- effective_from: 2026-10-01

- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory engineering standard
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. RAG source controls

Use owner-approved sources with stable document/section/version IDs, effective dates, hashes and permissions. Preserve exclusions and cross-references during parsing. Maintain a source manifest and reject mixed or superseded current snapshots. Historical reconstruction uses the exact historical snapshot.

## S02. Retrieval design

For the AI Compass project compare dense, BM25 and hybrid retrieval. Initial candidate design is dense top 8 plus lexical top 8, RRF fusion, deduplication, optional reranking and parent/cross-reference expansion. These are project configuration choices, not mandatory settings for every enterprise application.

## S03. Evaluation metrics and targets

For the fictional AI Compass release, target required-section Recall@5 >=0.90, claim faithfulness >=0.95, citation precision >=0.95, correct abstention >=0.90 and p95 complete-response latency <=10 seconds. Also report false abstention, citation completeness, restriction coverage, usefulness and cost. Report counts and denominators; targets are not measured results.

## S04. Dataset and judge controls

Use 50 labeled questions: 15 direct, 10 multi-source, 10 missing-context, 10 unanswerable/conflict and 5 adversarial. Use 30 development and 20 held-out cases, keeping paraphrase families in one split. Gold labels must be reviewed. Calibrate judges against human samples and keep evaluator/model versions. Do not tune on the holdout.

## S05. Release evidence

Attach a configuration manifest, evaluated dataset version, raw outputs, metric numerators/denominators, failure disposition, access-control tests, incident/rollback plan and oversight ownership. A synthetic fixture is never proof that actual model or security tests ran. Required pre-release evidence must be independently verified for the exact request version.

## S06. Change validation

Changing generation, embedding or reranking models, prompts, chunking, corpus, permissions, hosting or integrations requires impact assessment and relevant regressions. Preserve old indexes until migration validation passes. A new model version does not inherit authorization automatically.

## S07. Monitoring and response

Track unsupported claims, prohibited guidance, missing evidence, stale sources, retrieval misses, latency and cost. Assign operations owners. A critical data-exposure signal triggers Security Incident intake and may revoke clearance. Never copy exposed payloads into monitoring or evaluation datasets unnecessarily.

## S08. Operational controls

Validate identity and case/document scope before retrieval, expansions, model calls and exports. Use parameterized queries and allowlisted tools. Validate state transitions server-side, apply idempotency keys and version checks, and append business events in the same transaction or through a transactional outbox.

## S09. Human oversight and retention

Define human handoff, release authority, rollback and manual fallback. In the fictional schedule retain case/evaluation evidence for 24 months after closure, longer under legal hold. LangSmith traces and application audit records serve different purposes; configure approved redaction and retention separately.

Decision owner plus affected policy owner and all base required domain reviewers must approve a time-bound exception. Maximum 90 days. The requester may not be an approver. Absolute prohibitions remain in force.

Requester must differ from final decision owner. Evidence submitter must differ from independent verifier. Audit is read-only. A sponsor, coordinator or administrator has only assigned authority. The model cannot create its own authority or determine a final decision.

# Enterprise AI Acceptable Use Policy

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 1
- source_id: POL-001
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: AI Governance
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory activity policy
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Scope and approval boundary

This policy covers employees, contractors and teams using AI for Northstar work. Permission is the intersection of activity, exact tool/model/deployment combination, purpose, data class, user population and approval conditions. Approval of an underlying model never authorizes an unlisted endpoint or a new customer-facing deployment. Use REG-002 for asset permissions and AUTH-009 for review authority.

## S02. Permitted everyday assistance

Within an existing approved combination, employees may draft, summarize, brainstorm, analyze permitted aggregate information and obtain code assistance. Routine use within recorded purpose and data limits needs tool access but no new use-case review. Review generated output before using it in a business process or communicating externally.

## S03. Absolute prohibitions

Do not use AI to make autonomous hiring, termination, credit or disciplinary decisions. Do not upload credentials, payment card details, production secrets, individual health records or individual HR performance records to any deployment in this corpus. No exception under PROC-004 may override these prohibitions.

## S04. Customer-facing and custom applications

New customer-facing generation, custom RAG applications, new system integrations and automated consequential advice require documented use-case review. A tool subscription, a pilot designation and sponsor endorsement do not grant production authorization. Release requires an applicable decision plus verified pre-release conditions.

## S05. Account and deployment requirements

Use company-managed identities, approved endpoints and required logging/retention settings. Personal consumer accounts are not permitted for company work. Do not copy an approved model name into an unapproved service and assume permission carries over. Unlisted tools have no documented approval.

## S06. Human accountability

The named employee remains responsible for accuracy, fairness and suitability. Customer communications require a competent reviewer. Generated code follows code review, testing and security checks. Legal interpretations require Legal review. The assistant provides guidance, not a formal approval or legal opinion.

## S07. Data handling

STD-003 determines classification and redaction. Raw personal data is excluded from every currently approved deployment in REG-002. Removing names alone does not establish anonymity. An approved Confidential nonpersonal use does not permit Confidential personal data.

## S08. Material change and renewal

A model-version change, new data class, region, provider, purpose, integration or audience requires change assessment under RSK-006. An earlier decision is scoped to its exact request version; a superseding version must not silently inherit affected reviews or release clearance. Expired, revoked and rejected decisions do not authorize continuing use.

## S09. Conflicts and missing evidence

Apply every relevant restriction. FAQ-005 is illustrative and cannot override authoritative rules. When authoritative sources conflict on the same requirement, identify the conflict, withhold definitive permission and contact the owners. Missing evidence, unknown regional approval and a low similarity score never imply permission.

## S10. Reporting and recordkeeping

Report suspected sensitive-data exposure immediately through Security Incident intake. Do not paste the exposed data into AI Compass. Record approval rationale, source versions and evidence references; log formal actions under AUD-012. Retain records under ENG-007 and PROC-004.

# Data Classification & AI Handling Standard

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 3
- source_id: STD-003
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: Information Security & Privacy
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory data standard
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Classification approach

The data owner assigns the highest applicable class. Evaluate content, context and linkability rather than file extension or size. A summary, embedding or pilot copy does not automatically lower classification. When classification is uncertain, ask the data owner or Security before upload.

## S02. Public

Information formally approved for public release, such as published product guides and public blog posts. It may be processed only in an approved combination for its permitted purpose. Public status does not remove intellectual-property or accuracy-review responsibilities.

## S03. Internal

Routine nonpublic agendas, nonsensitive operating instructions and truly aggregate sales figures without customer-level records. Use company identities and deployments explicitly permitting Internal data. The source owner must confirm that aggregation removes identifiers and small-group reidentification risks.

## S04. Confidential nonpersonal

Nonpublic commercial plans, contracts without personal information, and source code without credentials, secrets or personal information. Only DEP-002 and DEP-003 permit specified Confidential nonpersonal uses; the approved purpose still applies. InsightDesk and Northstar Assist do not permit Confidential data.

## S05. Confidential personal

Customer names, email addresses, identifiable support transcripts and supplier contact details are Confidential personal data unless a higher class applies. All currently approved deployments exclude raw personal data. Privacy review alone does not grant permission where the catalog or policy still prohibits processing.

## S06. Restricted

Credentials, payment card details, production secrets, individual health records and individual HR performance records are Restricted. No registered deployment may process them. The exception route cannot override this rule. Stop upload and involve the data owner or Security.

## S07. Redaction and reassessment

Remove direct identifiers and indirect identifiers, unique account/order references, sensitive free text and details enabling reidentification. Reassess the remaining content with the owner. Routine meeting notes may become Internal only if no Confidential or Restricted information remains. Use synthetic examples when sanitization cannot be established.

## S08. RAG and derived artifacts

Source ACLs and classification apply to extracted text, chunks, embeddings, indexes, reranker inputs, retrieved context, evaluation datasets, traces and exports. Enforce authorization before retrieval and on parent expansion, evidence display and download. Do not expose excluded text to an external judge or reranker.

## S09. Regional scope

Catalog endpoints in this corpus are approved only for their recorded fictional region and environment. No blanket EU, Austria, APAC or cross-border permission is documented. Route regional questions to Privacy, Legal and Architecture; do not infer a legal conclusion.

## S10. Exposure response

If prohibited data was entered into a tool, stop further use, notify Security Incident intake, preserve relevant record identifiers and follow the incident owner instructions. Do not ask an assistant to repeat, recover or redistribute the exposed material.

# AI Access & Exception Procedure

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 4
- source_id: PROC-004
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: AI Governance Operations
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory operating procedure
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Approved-tool access

Submit tool/deployment ID, purpose, manager and intended data categories to IT Service Desk. Check the exact permitted combination first. Access target is two business days after a complete request; service targets are not guarantees or automatic approvals.

## S02. Use-case intake

Provide purpose, requester, sponsor, users, tools, all generation/embedding/reranking model versions, endpoints, hosting region, data classes/flows, oversight, impact and evaluation plan. Submit categories, not raw sensitive examples. Submission freezes a numbered snapshot.

## S03. Triage and information requests

Governance checks completeness, confirms the risk screening and applies AUTH-009. Triage target is three business days after complete intake. Missing information pauses triage or review; the coordinator records the requested fields and accountable owner. Do not treat an overdue target as approval.

## S04. Domain review and blockers

Assigned specialists record satisfactory, changes-requested or blocking findings for a specific request version. They cite requirements and evidence. A domain finding is not final disposition. Required unsatisfactory findings prevent approval; the decision owner cannot silently override them.

## S05. Formal decisions

Only the assigned authorized decision owner records Approved, Approved with conditions, Rejected or Return for revision. Record rationale, exact scope, applicable policy/routing versions, validity and conditions. Requesters may not decide their own cases. A sponsor or administrator has no implied decision authority.

## S06. Exceptions

Name the requirement, business need, compensating control, risk owner, duration and policy owner. Permitted exceptions last at most 90 days and need the decision owner plus affected policy-owner approval. Exceptions cannot permit Restricted data, personal accounts, autonomous prohibited decisions or raw personal data in a deployment that excludes it.

## S07. Evidence and release

Separate pre-release conditions from ongoing obligations. Evidence owners submit versioned artifacts; a distinct assigned verifier inspects them against the exact configuration. Only the release authority clears the case after all pre-release conditions pass. Ongoing monitoring remains required after release.

## S08. Change, renewal, expiry and revocation

Open a new request version for material scope changes. Reopen affected reviews. Renew before the valid-until timestamp; after expiry stop the scoped activity until reauthorization. Security or Governance may revoke an approval through a recorded decision; preserve original history.

## S09. Escalation and incidents

Policy ambiguity: AI Governance Operations. Data classification: data owner or Security. Proposed personal data: Privacy plus catalog-owner assessment. Suspected exposure: Security Incident intake immediately. All named teams and internal routes are fictional service records in this corpus.

## S10. Records, corrections and retention

Keep immutable submitted snapshots and append superseding decisions with reasons. Retain records for 24 months after closure in this fictional schedule, extended by legal hold. Restrict cases and exports by assignment. Record timestamps in UTC. History integrity requires server controls; synthetic hashes are demonstrations only.

# AI Usage FAQ & Worked Examples

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 5
- source_id: FAQ-005
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: Employee Enablement
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Illustrative; never overrides authoritative rules
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Can AI draft a customer email?

Yes, within DEP-001 limits. Use Public or Internal nonpersonal inputs and have a competent employee review before sending.

Governing citations: POL-001@3.0:S02, POL-001@3.0:S06, REG-002@3.0:DEP-001.

## S02. Can I upload a spreadsheet with customer names and emails?

No currently approved deployment permits raw personal data. Removing the name column alone is not sufficient redaction.

Governing citations: STD-003@3.0:S05, STD-003@3.0:S07, REG-002@3.0:S01.

## S03. Can I summarize a nonpublic contract?

Use DEP-003 only for Confidential nonpersonal contract summarization. Remove personal data and secrets; Legal validates interpretations.

Governing citations: STD-003@3.0:S04, REG-002@3.0:DEP-003, POL-001@3.0:S06.

## S04. Can I paste an API key into CodeForge to debug an error?

No. Credentials are Restricted even when source code itself is permitted.

Governing citations: POL-001@3.0:S03, STD-003@3.0:S06, REG-002@3.0:DEP-002.

## S05. Which tool can analyze aggregate weekly sales?

InsightDesk DEP-004 can analyze Public or Internal aggregate data. Customer-level personal records are excluded.

Governing citations: REG-002@3.0:DEP-004, STD-003@3.0:S03, STD-003@3.0:S05.

## S06. Does a model approval authorize our chatbot?

No. A custom customer-facing application needs the exact deployment and case approval, required reviews and release evidence.

Governing citations: POL-001@3.0:S01, AUTH-009@3.0:S02, ENG-007@3.0:S05.

## S07. Can I use my personal account for routine company notes?

No. Company work requires the approved company account and deployment.

Governing citations: POL-001@3.0:S05.

## S08. Can a pilot bypass the approval rules?

No. Pilot-only status limits users and purpose; it does not authorize production, prohibited data or autonomous consequential decisions.

Governing citations: REG-002@3.0:S02, POL-001@3.0:S03, RSK-006@3.0:S06.

## S09. How do I get access to Northstar Assist?

Confirm DEP-001 scope, then send purpose, manager and data categories to IT Service Desk. Target is two business days after complete intake, not a guarantee.

Governing citations: PROC-004@3.0:S01, REG-002@3.0:DEP-001.

## S10. What if the requested tool is not in the register?

Do not infer approval. Prepare a new-tool/use-case intake and wait for the relevant assessment.

Governing citations: POL-001@3.0:S05, PROC-004@3.0:S02.

## S11. Can AI make a hiring shortlist from individual performance reviews?

Autonomous hiring decisions are prohibited and individual performance records are Restricted. A case exception cannot authorize the proposal.

Governing citations: POL-001@3.0:S03, STD-003@3.0:S06, AUTH-009@3.0:S05.

## S12. Can we change Vector Pine 1.0 to 1.1 without reapproval?

No. MOD-008@1.1 and DEP-011 are under review; use a separate index, impact assessment and regression evidence.

Governing citations: REG-002@3.0:MOD-008@1.1, REG-002@3.0:DEP-011, ENG-007@3.0:S06.

## S13. Who can give final approval?

The assigned authorized decision owner, after mandatory reviews. Sponsor, coordinator and administrator status alone are insufficient.

Governing citations: PROC-004@3.0:S05, AUTH-009@3.0:S08.

## S14. Can the person uploading evidence verify it too?

No. A distinct assigned independent verifier must inspect the exact artifact/configuration.

Governing citations: PROC-004@3.0:S07, AUTH-009@3.0:S08.

## S15. Does conditional approval mean ready for production?

No. All pre-release conditions must pass and release authority must record clearance. Ongoing obligations continue after release.

Governing citations: AUTH-009@3.0:S09, PROC-004@3.0:S07.

## S16. Can an approved model be used in a new overseas region?

No regional permission can be established from this corpus beyond US-SYN-1. Ask Privacy, Legal and Architecture; do not assume authorization.

Governing citations: STD-003@3.0:S09, REG-002@3.0:S01.

## S17. What if two policies conflict?

Identify the conflicting requirements, abstain from definitive permission and contact the source owners. FAQ examples cannot override authoritative rules.

Governing citations: POL-001@3.0:S09.

## S18. Can I keep using an application after approval expires?

No. Renew before expiration; stop scoped use after expiry until reauthorization.

Governing citations: PROC-004@3.0:S08, AUTH-009@3.0:S09.

## S19. Will a read-only source ACL still apply to embeddings?

Yes. Classification and source permissions apply to chunks, embeddings, retrieval context, reranker inputs and exports.

Governing citations: STD-003@3.0:S08, ENG-007@3.0:S01.

## S20. Can an LLM judge approve release evidence?

It can assist evaluation, but it cannot act as the authorized human verifier or decision owner. Synthetic fixtures are not proof of actual test execution.

Governing citations: AUTH-009@3.0:S08, ENG-007@3.0:S05.

# AI Use Case Risk Assessment & Review Standard

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 6
- source_id: RSK-006
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: Enterprise Risk & AI Governance
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory assessment standard
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Screening outcomes

Low: assistance wholly inside an existing approved combination and purpose. Moderate: new internal custom applications or integrations without prohibited data. High: customer-facing generation or material consequential advice requiring accountable human oversight. Prohibited: any activity expressly barred by POL-001. These are fictional enterprise categories, not regulatory classifications.

## S02. Context and accountability

Record affected users, output use, business impact, data lineage, intended oversight and fallback. The assistant may suggest a tier, but Governance confirms screening. Consider the application behavior, not merely the model size or vendor reputation.

## S03. Customer-facing builds

Require sponsor endorsement and Technology, Security, Legal and Compliance/Risk reviews. Add Privacy when personal data is proposed. A missing Privacy assessment blocks a personal-data proposal, and a Privacy finding cannot override a catalog data restriction. Use AUTH-009 rules R02 and R04.

## S04. Internal custom builds

Require sponsor endorsement and Technology and Security reviews. Add Legal for contractual/IP interpretation and Privacy for proposed personal data. Routine existing tool use within scope is not a custom build. Use AUTH-009 rules R01 and R03.

## S05. Model and deployment changes

Evaluate generation, embedding and reranking versions separately. Changing the embedding model requires a separate consistent index and retrieval reevaluation; do not mix vector spaces. Model/provider/endpoint/region changes require a recorded assessment. See ENG-007 S06.

## S06. Conditions and residual risk

Describe compensating controls, owner, evidence, phase, due date and monitoring. A pre-release condition is not satisfied by promising to fix it later. Ongoing obligations remain tracked after clearance. A prohibited activity cannot be downgraded to Low through a pilot or exception.

## S07. Reassessment triggers

New users, data categories, system integration, autonomous behavior, material retrieval/prompt changes, security incidents and expiring authority trigger reassessment. The new snapshot must reference previous versions and identify which reviews remain applicable; affected reviews must be redone.

## S08. Worked screening examples

Public blog drafting in DEP-001: Low. New internal RAG application in proposed DEP-009: Moderate. Existing contract summary in DEP-003 within purpose: Low. Customer support RAG application: High. Confidential nonpersonal code in DEP-002 within purpose: Low. Autonomous hiring selection: Prohibited.

# AI Development, Evaluation & Monitoring Standard

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 7
- source_id: ENG-007
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: AI Engineering & Quality
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory engineering standard
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. RAG source controls

Use owner-approved sources with stable document/section/version IDs, effective dates, hashes and permissions. Preserve exclusions and cross-references during parsing. Maintain a source manifest and reject mixed or superseded current snapshots. Historical reconstruction uses the exact historical snapshot.

## S02. Retrieval design

For the AI Compass project compare dense, BM25 and hybrid retrieval. Initial candidate design is dense top 8 plus lexical top 8, RRF fusion, deduplication, optional reranking and parent/cross-reference expansion. These are project configuration choices, not mandatory settings for every enterprise application.

## S03. Evaluation metrics and targets

For the fictional AI Compass release, target required-section Recall@5 >=0.90, claim faithfulness >=0.95, citation precision >=0.95, correct abstention >=0.90 and p95 complete-response latency <=10 seconds. Also report false abstention, citation completeness, restriction coverage, usefulness and cost. Report counts and denominators; targets are not measured results.

## S04. Dataset and judge controls

Use 50 labeled questions: 15 direct, 10 multi-source, 10 missing-context, 10 unanswerable/conflict and 5 adversarial. Use 30 development and 20 held-out cases, keeping paraphrase families in one split. Gold labels must be reviewed. Calibrate judges against human samples and keep evaluator/model versions. Do not tune on the holdout.

## S05. Release evidence

Attach a configuration manifest, evaluated dataset version, raw outputs, metric numerators/denominators, failure disposition, access-control tests, incident/rollback plan and oversight ownership. A synthetic fixture is never proof that actual model or security tests ran. Required pre-release evidence must be independently verified for the exact request version.

## S06. Change validation

Changing generation, embedding or reranking models, prompts, chunking, corpus, permissions, hosting or integrations requires impact assessment and relevant regressions. Preserve old indexes until migration validation passes. A new model version does not inherit authorization automatically.

## S07. Monitoring and response

Track unsupported claims, prohibited guidance, missing evidence, stale sources, retrieval misses, latency and cost. Assign operations owners. A critical data-exposure signal triggers Security Incident intake and may revoke clearance. Never copy exposed payloads into monitoring or evaluation datasets unnecessarily.

## S08. Operational controls

Validate identity and case/document scope before retrieval, expansions, model calls and exports. Use parameterized queries and allowlisted tools. Validate state transitions server-side, apply idempotency keys and version checks, and append business events in the same transaction or through a transactional outbox.

## S09. Human oversight and retention

Define human handoff, release authority, rollback and manual fallback. In the fictional schedule retain case/evaluation evidence for 24 months after closure, longer under legal hold. LangSmith traces and application audit records serve different purposes; configure approved redaction and retention separately.

## S01. R01. Existing approved use

When activity, data, tool/model/deployment and users all match an existing approval: tool-access request only, no new use-case decision. Manager endorses access; IT provisions. Data exclusions and employee human review remain mandatory.

## S02. R02. Customer-facing custom build

Require sponsor endorsement and satisfactory Technology, Security, Legal and Compliance/Risk findings. Add Privacy under R04 when personal data is proposed. Assigned Governance Decision Owner records disposition; the same assigned owner clears release after required verification. No elapsed-time or majority-vote approval.

## S03. R03. Internal custom build

Require sponsor endorsement, Technology and Security. Add Legal for contractual/IP interpretation and Privacy under R04 for proposed personal data. Governance confirms route. Decision owner: assigned Governance Decision Owner.

## S04. R04. Personal-data proposal

Add Privacy to the applicable route. Current approved deployments exclude raw personal data; keep a blocking finding until a permitted alternative scope or a properly authorized policy/catalog change exists. A case-level exception alone cannot override the catalog restriction.

## S05. R05. Prohibited activity

Governance records rejection with POL-001 S03 or STD-003 S06. Do not collect unnecessary data or run a full approval sequence to authorize a prohibited use. Stop the scoped proposal; discuss a materially different permitted alternative if requested.

## S06. R06. Change and renewal

Use the base route for the changed scope and re-review affected domains. Preserve prior version decisions. A model or embedding upgrade reopens Technology, Security and Quality evidence assessment; customer-facing scope keeps Legal and Compliance/Risk requirements. Renewals need current evidence, not a copied old date.

## S07. R07. Permitted exception

Decision owner plus affected policy owner and all base required domain reviewers must approve a time-bound exception. Maximum 90 days. The requester may not be an approver. Absolute prohibitions remain in force.

## S08. R08. Separation of duties

Requester must differ from final decision owner. Evidence submitter must differ from independent verifier. Audit is read-only. A sponsor, coordinator or administrator has only assigned authority. The model cannot create its own authority or determine a final decision.

## S09. R09. Release and expiration

Only Approved or Approved with conditions disposition in its effective interval can support clearance. Every applicable pre-release condition must be verified. An expired or revoked disposition blocks clearance and continuing scoped use. Ongoing conditions remain monitored.

## S10. R10. Access and escalation

Apply case assignment and document scope independently. A domain reviewer does not get access to every company case. Coordinators manage missing information and escalate due dates. An escalation is not permission to skip a mandatory review.

# Enterprise AI Acceptable Use Policy

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 1
- source_id: POL-001
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: AI Governance
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory activity policy
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Scope and approval boundary

This policy covers employees, contractors and teams using AI for Northstar work. Permission is the intersection of activity, exact tool/model/deployment combination, purpose, data class, user population and approval conditions. Approval of an underlying model never authorizes an unlisted endpoint or a new customer-facing deployment. Use REG-002 for asset permissions and AUTH-009 for review authority.

## S02. Permitted everyday assistance

Within an existing approved combination, employees may draft, summarize, brainstorm, analyze permitted aggregate information and obtain code assistance. Routine use within recorded purpose and data limits needs tool access but no new use-case review. Review generated output before using it in a business process or communicating externally.

## S03. Absolute prohibitions

Do not use AI to make autonomous hiring, termination, credit or disciplinary decisions. Do not upload credentials, payment card details, production secrets, individual health records or individual HR performance records to any deployment in this corpus. No exception under PROC-004 may override these prohibitions.

## S04. Customer-facing and custom applications

New customer-facing generation, custom RAG applications, new system integrations and automated consequential advice require documented use-case review. A tool subscription, a pilot designation and sponsor endorsement do not grant production authorization. Release requires an applicable decision plus verified pre-release conditions.

## S05. Account and deployment requirements

Use company-managed identities, approved endpoints and required logging/retention settings. Personal consumer accounts are not permitted for company work. Do not copy an approved model name into an unapproved service and assume permission carries over. Unlisted tools have no documented approval.

## S06. Human accountability

The named employee remains responsible for accuracy, fairness and suitability. Customer communications require a competent reviewer. Generated code follows code review, testing and security checks. Legal interpretations require Legal review. The assistant provides guidance, not a formal approval or legal opinion.

## S07. Data handling

STD-003 determines classification and redaction. Raw personal data is excluded from every currently approved deployment in REG-002. Removing names alone does not establish anonymity. An approved Confidential nonpersonal use does not permit Confidential personal data.

## S08. Material change and renewal

A model-version change, new data class, region, provider, purpose, integration or audience requires change assessment under RSK-006. An earlier decision is scoped to its exact request version; a superseding version must not silently inherit affected reviews or release clearance. Expired, revoked and rejected decisions do not authorize continuing use.

## S09. Conflicts and missing evidence

Apply every relevant restriction. FAQ-005 is illustrative and cannot override authoritative rules. When authoritative sources conflict on the same requirement, identify the conflict, withhold definitive permission and contact the owners. Missing evidence, unknown regional approval and a low similarity score never imply permission.

## S10. Reporting and recordkeeping

Report suspected sensitive-data exposure immediately through Security Incident intake. Do not paste the exposed data into AI Compass. Record approval rationale, source versions and evidence references; log formal actions under AUD-012. Retain records under ENG-007 and PROC-004.

# Data Classification & AI Handling Standard

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 3
- source_id: STD-003
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: Information Security & Privacy
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory data standard
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Classification approach

The data owner assigns the highest applicable class. Evaluate content, context and linkability rather than file extension or size. A summary, embedding or pilot copy does not automatically lower classification. When classification is uncertain, ask the data owner or Security before upload.

## S02. Public

Information formally approved for public release, such as published product guides and public blog posts. It may be processed only in an approved combination for its permitted purpose. Public status does not remove intellectual-property or accuracy-review responsibilities.

## S03. Internal

Routine nonpublic agendas, nonsensitive operating instructions and truly aggregate sales figures without customer-level records. Use company identities and deployments explicitly permitting Internal data. The source owner must confirm that aggregation removes identifiers and small-group reidentification risks.

## S04. Confidential nonpersonal

Nonpublic commercial plans, contracts without personal information, and source code without credentials, secrets or personal information. Only DEP-002 and DEP-003 permit specified Confidential nonpersonal uses; the approved purpose still applies. InsightDesk and Northstar Assist do not permit Confidential data.

## S05. Confidential personal

Customer names, email addresses, identifiable support transcripts and supplier contact details are Confidential personal data unless a higher class applies. All currently approved deployments exclude raw personal data. Privacy review alone does not grant permission where the catalog or policy still prohibits processing.

## S06. Restricted

Credentials, payment card details, production secrets, individual health records and individual HR performance records are Restricted. No registered deployment may process them. The exception route cannot override this rule. Stop upload and involve the data owner or Security.

## S07. Redaction and reassessment

Remove direct identifiers and indirect identifiers, unique account/order references, sensitive free text and details enabling reidentification. Reassess the remaining content with the owner. Routine meeting notes may become Internal only if no Confidential or Restricted information remains. Use synthetic examples when sanitization cannot be established.

## S08. RAG and derived artifacts

Source ACLs and classification apply to extracted text, chunks, embeddings, indexes, reranker inputs, retrieved context, evaluation datasets, traces and exports. Enforce authorization before retrieval and on parent expansion, evidence display and download. Do not expose excluded text to an external judge or reranker.

## S09. Regional scope

Catalog endpoints in this corpus are approved only for their recorded fictional region and environment. No blanket EU, Austria, APAC or cross-border permission is documented. Route regional questions to Privacy, Legal and Architecture; do not infer a legal conclusion.

## S10. Exposure response

If prohibited data was entered into a tool, stop further use, notify Security Incident intake, preserve relevant record identifiers and follow the incident owner instructions. Do not ask an assistant to repeat, recover or redistribute the exposed material.

# AI Access & Exception Procedure

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 4
- source_id: PROC-004
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: AI Governance Operations
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory operating procedure
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Approved-tool access

Submit tool/deployment ID, purpose, manager and intended data categories to IT Service Desk. Check the exact permitted combination first. Access target is two business days after a complete request; service targets are not guarantees or automatic approvals.

## S02. Use-case intake

Provide purpose, requester, sponsor, users, tools, all generation/embedding/reranking model versions, endpoints, hosting region, data classes/flows, oversight, impact and evaluation plan. Submit categories, not raw sensitive examples. Submission freezes a numbered snapshot.

## S03. Triage and information requests

Governance checks completeness, confirms the risk screening and applies AUTH-009. Triage target is three business days after complete intake. Missing information pauses triage or review; the coordinator records the requested fields and accountable owner. Do not treat an overdue target as approval.

## S04. Domain review and blockers

Assigned specialists record satisfactory, changes-requested or blocking findings for a specific request version. They cite requirements and evidence. A domain finding is not final disposition. Required unsatisfactory findings prevent approval; the decision owner cannot silently override them.

## S05. Formal decisions

Only the assigned authorized decision owner records Approved, Approved with conditions, Rejected or Return for revision. Record rationale, exact scope, applicable policy/routing versions, validity and conditions. Requesters may not decide their own cases. A sponsor or administrator has no implied decision authority.

## S06. Exceptions

Name the requirement, business need, compensating control, risk owner, duration and policy owner. Permitted exceptions last at most 90 days and need the decision owner plus affected policy-owner approval. Exceptions cannot permit Restricted data, personal accounts, autonomous prohibited decisions or raw personal data in a deployment that excludes it.

## S07. Evidence and release

Separate pre-release conditions from ongoing obligations. Evidence owners submit versioned artifacts; a distinct assigned verifier inspects them against the exact configuration. Only the release authority clears the case after all pre-release conditions pass. Ongoing monitoring remains required after release.

## S08. Change, renewal, expiry and revocation

Open a new request version for material scope changes. Reopen affected reviews. Renew before the valid-until timestamp; after expiry stop the scoped activity until reauthorization. Security or Governance may revoke an approval through a recorded decision; preserve original history.

## S09. Escalation and incidents

Policy ambiguity: AI Governance Operations. Data classification: data owner or Security. Proposed personal data: Privacy plus catalog-owner assessment. Suspected exposure: Security Incident intake immediately. All named teams and internal routes are fictional service records in this corpus.

## S10. Records, corrections and retention

Keep immutable submitted snapshots and append superseding decisions with reasons. Retain records for 24 months after closure in this fictional schedule, extended by legal hold. Restrict cases and exports by assignment. Record timestamps in UTC. History integrity requires server controls; synthetic hashes are demonstrations only.

Confirm DEP-001 scope, then send purpose, manager and data categories to IT Service Desk. Target is two business days after complete intake, not a guarantee.

The assigned authorized decision owner, after mandatory reviews. Sponsor, coordinator and administrator status alone are insufficient.

Governing citations: PROC-004@3.0:S05, AUTH-009@3.0:S08.

## S14. Can the person uploading evidence verify it too?

No. A distinct assigned independent verifier must inspect the exact artifact/configuration.

Governing citations: PROC-004@3.0:S07, AUTH-009@3.0:S08.

No. All pre-release conditions must pass and release authority must record clearance. Ongoing obligations continue after release.

No regional permission can be established from this corpus beyond US-SYN-1. Ask Privacy, Legal and Architecture; do not assume authorization.

Governing citations: STD-003@3.0:S09, REG-002@3.0:S01.

Identify the conflicting requirements, abstain from definitive permission and contact the source owners. FAQ examples cannot override authoritative rules.

# AI Use Case Risk Assessment & Review Standard

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- authority: Mandatory assessment standard
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. Screening outcomes

Low: assistance wholly inside an existing approved combination and purpose. Moderate: new internal custom applications or integrations without prohibited data. High: customer-facing generation or material consequential advice requiring accountable human oversight. Prohibited: any activity expressly barred by POL-001. These are fictional enterprise categories, not regulatory classifications.

## S02. Context and accountability

Record affected users, output use, business impact, data lineage, intended oversight and fallback. The assistant may suggest a tier, but Governance confirms screening. Consider the application behavior, not merely the model size or vendor reputation.

## S03. Customer-facing builds

Require sponsor endorsement and Technology, Security, Legal and Compliance/Risk reviews. Add Privacy when personal data is proposed. A missing Privacy assessment blocks a personal-data proposal, and a Privacy finding cannot override a catalog data restriction. Use AUTH-009 rules R02 and R04.

## S04. Internal custom builds

Require sponsor endorsement and Technology and Security reviews. Add Legal for contractual/IP interpretation and Privacy for proposed personal data. Routine existing tool use within scope is not a custom build. Use AUTH-009 rules R01 and R03.

## S05. Model and deployment changes

Evaluate generation, embedding and reranking versions separately. Changing the embedding model requires a separate consistent index and retrieval reevaluation; do not mix vector spaces. Model/provider/endpoint/region changes require a recorded assessment. See ENG-007 S06.

## S06. Conditions and residual risk

Describe compensating controls, owner, evidence, phase, due date and monitoring. A pre-release condition is not satisfied by promising to fix it later. Ongoing obligations remain tracked after clearance. A prohibited activity cannot be downgraded to Low through a pilot or exception.

## S07. Reassessment triggers

New users, data categories, system integration, autonomous behavior, material retrieval/prompt changes, security incidents and expiring authority trigger reassessment. The new snapshot must reference previous versions and identify which reviews remain applicable; affected reviews must be redone.

## S08. Worked screening examples

Public blog drafting in DEP-001: Low. New internal RAG application in proposed DEP-009: Moderate. Existing contract summary in DEP-003 within purpose: Low. Customer support RAG application: High. Confidential nonpersonal code in DEP-002 within purpose: Low. Autonomous hiring selection: Prohibited.

# AI Development, Evaluation & Monitoring Standard

SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. Northstar Enterprises is fictional. Not a real company policy or legal guidance.

- source_number: 7
- source_id: ENG-007
- version: 3.0
- effective_from: 2026-10-01
- status: published
- owner: AI Engineering & Quality
- approving_authority: Northstar AI Governance Council
- authority: Mandatory engineering standard
- snapshot_at: 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z
- Access: employee-visible policy; operational case access is separate.

## S01. RAG source controls

Use owner-approved sources with stable document/section/version IDs, effective dates, hashes and permissions. Preserve exclusions and cross-references during parsing. Maintain a source manifest and reject mixed or superseded current snapshots. Historical reconstruction uses the exact historical snapshot.

## S02. Retrieval design

For the AI Compass project compare dense, BM25 and hybrid retrieval. Initial candidate design is dense top 8 plus lexical top 8, RRF fusion, deduplication, optional reranking and parent/cross-reference expansion. These are project configuration choices, not mandatory settings for every enterprise application.

## S03. Evaluation metrics and targets

For the fictional AI Compass release, target required-section Recall@5 >=0.90, claim faithfulness >=0.95, citation precision >=0.95, correct abstention >=0.90 and p95 complete-response latency <=10 seconds. Also report false abstention, citation completeness, restriction coverage, usefulness and cost. Report counts and denominators; targets are not measured results.

## S04. Dataset and judge controls

Use 50 labeled questions: 15 direct, 10 multi-source, 10 missing-context, 10 unanswerable/conflict and 5 adversarial. Use 30 development and 20 held-out cases, keeping paraphrase families in one split. Gold labels must be reviewed. Calibrate judges against human samples and keep evaluator/model versions. Do not tune on the holdout.

## S05. Release evidence

Attach a configuration manifest, evaluated dataset version, raw outputs, metric numerators/denominators, failure disposition, access-control tests, incident/rollback plan and oversight ownership. A synthetic fixture is never proof that actual model or security tests ran. Required pre-release evidence must be independently verified for the exact request version.

## S06. Change validation

Changing generation, embedding or reranking models, prompts, chunking, corpus, permissions, hosting or integrations requires impact assessment and relevant regressions. Preserve old indexes until migration validation passes. A new model version does not inherit authorization automatically.

## S07. Monitoring and response

Track unsupported claims, prohibited guidance, missing evidence, stale sources, retrieval misses, latency and cost. Assign operations owners. A critical data-exposure signal triggers Security Incident intake and may revoke clearance. Never copy exposed payloads into monitoring or evaluation datasets unnecessarily.

## S08. Operational controls

Validate identity and case/document scope before retrieval, expansions, model calls and exports. Use parameterized queries and allowlisted tools. Validate state transitions server-side, apply idempotency keys and version checks, and append business events in the same transaction or through a transactional outbox.

## S09. Human oversight and retention

Define human handoff, release authority, rollback and manual fallback. In the fictional schedule retain case/evaluation evidence for 24 months after closure, longer under legal hold. LangSmith traces and application audit records serve different purposes; configure approved redaction and retention separately.

Decision owner plus affected policy owner and all base required domain reviewers must approve a time-bound exception. Maximum 90 days. The requester may not be an approver. Absolute prohibitions remain in force.
